mainEntity.name: How does an attached in-law suite compare to a detached accessory dwelling unit (ADU)?

acceptedAnswer.text: An attached suite is physically connected to the main house, sharing foundational and structural elements, while a detached accessory dwelling unit (ADU) is a standalone structure on your property. Choosing between them involves balancing lot space, privacy, and budget. Attached additions often integrate more affordably with existing plumbing, electrical, and HVAC lines, and provide immediate indoor access to assist aging relatives. In contrast, detached units offer maximum privacy and sound separation but require sufficient yard space and independent utility connections, which increases project complexity.
acceptedAnswer.description: Attached suites connect directly to the main home for easier care access and shared utilities, while detached ADUs provide independent standalone privacy on larger lots.
